title: Generative AI and the Crisis of Higher Education Assessments: Examining 'AI-Proofing' Strategies for College-Level Assessments
abstract: arXiv:2611.21476v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Higher education is confronting an academic-integrity challenge unlike any in its history. Students can now outsource homework, take-home assignments, and online examinations to large language models (LLMs) that complete them in seconds. Existing research on evaluating LLM performance on academic assessments has focused largely on standardized examinations, or on questions from college-level courses drawn from a single discipline. Far less is known about how LLMs perform on college-level assessment questions spanning multiple disciplines, that instructors have purposely designed to be AI-resistant, and about which features of such questions, if any, meaningfully constrain LLM performance. We address this gap by collecting 75 questions from authentic college coursework assessments, spanning 17 disciplines, which were contributed by 37 faculty members from ten U.S. universities and one U.K. university. translated_title: 生成式人工智能与高等教育评估危机：审视大学层面评估的“抗AI”策略
translated_abstract: 高等教育正面临其历史上前所未有的学术诚信挑战。学生现在可以将课后作业、家庭作业和在线考试外包给大型语言模型（LLM），这些模型能在几秒钟内完成这些任务。现有关于评估LLM在学术测评中表现的研究主要集中于标准化考试，或来自单一学科的大学课程题目。而关于LLM在跨多个学科、由教师有意设计为抗AI的大学评估题目上的表现，以及这类题目的哪些特征（如果存在的话）能够有效约束LLM的表现，目前所知甚少。我们通过收集75道来自真实大学课程评估的题目来填补这一空白，这些题目涵盖17个学科，由来自美国十所大学和英国一所大学的37名教师提供。其中，61道题目是刻意设计为（抗AI的）……
tldr: 该研究收集了来自17个学科、由11所大学37名教师贡献的75道真实大学课程评估题目（其中61道刻意设计为抗AI），以考察大型语言模型在多学科大学评估中的表现，并探究哪些题目特征能有效约束LLM的性能。
en_tdlr: This study collected 75 authentic college assessment questions across 17 disciplines, contributed by 37 faculty members from 11 universities (with 61 deliberately designed to be AI-resistant), to examine how LLMs perform on multi-disciplinary college assessments and which question features meaningfully constrain LLM performance.
